audit.what: The flagged dataset fallback is benign: the GitHub clone failed and it fell back to the real HF allenai/IFBench_test, 300 rows. But the reward never checks IFBench instructions. constraint_params is always {}, so constraint_adherence just buckets word or paragraph counts, and the other 0.4 weight is generic formatting.
audit.evidence: ifbench.py:564-578 wrapper only sets constraint_params if `answer.get` (answer is a str) or `completion.get` (completion is a list), so it is always `{}`; :479-520 then returns length buckets (e.g. `if len(words) < 5: return 0.1 ... else 0.8`); :522-562 format_quality = word count, newlines, capitalisation, trailing punctuation; :584-590 weights [0.6, 0.3, 0.1]. The IFBench verifier code (only in the GitHub repo) is never imported. load.log shows the clone failed, then HF fallback, 300 rows. Constant 0.34 reward for the mock.
audit.user_impact: Scores reflect response length and paragraphing, not instruction following. A long multi-paragraph answer that ignores every constraint scores about 0.8+, so RL on it optimizes verbosity. Results are not comparable to IFBench.

gold_review.explanation: Constraint parameters never reach the scorer (answer is the constraint-id string and completion is a list, so constraint_params is always {}), so constraint_adherence falls back to pure word/paragraph-count buckets and the other 40% is length/capitalization/punctuation formatting — no reward term checks whether the instruction was actually followed. (Answer itself is the constraint id, not a response.)
gold_review.evidence: ifbench.py:564-578 constraint_params only from answer.get/completion.get → {}; :482-520 word-count/paragraph-count fallbacks; :522-562 format_quality = length/newlines/capitalization; :590 weights [0.6,0.3,0.1]; gold and garbage both r1=[0.34]*5
